acceptance: Each registered assertion must pass; failures/denials and deliberate unsafe diagnostic effects remain outcomes. This is instrument acceptance, not deployment or population C/R/E acceptance.
cost: Count actual local signature checks/hash reads/policy operations; record local elapsed time separately. No tariffs, salaries or production SLA inferred.

coverage.correspondence: declared local realization, no operational isomorphism proved
coverage.M: explicitly allowed lower-value outcome only when chosen/completed
coverage.incomplete: no sufficient route within the registered horizon
coverage.probability_law: designed finite cases; no population probability fitted
coverage.business_value: illustrative process objective; owner calibration pending

private_state: Expected flags and actual-world facts belong only to the evaluator; participant functions receive observations/claims and admitted current policy sources.
credential_policy: Ephemeral fixture signing keys and compact tokens remain in memory; no credential or private key in output.
implementation_profile: SPIFFE JWT-SVID RS256 local validation and qualified batch receiver

cases.narrative: A valid client presents a token for the intended batch endpoint.
The intended service is one entry in a multi-audience credential.
A validly signed identity token is addressed to another service.
The service receives the credential exactly at its expiry.
A credential has no audience.
A credential has no expiration.
An untrusted issuer uses a familiar key name.
A key identifier is absent from the admitted bundle.
A header names a symmetric algorithm outside this selected RSA profile.
A token tries to supply its own remote key location.
A signature-valid payload repeats an expiration member.
The subject is an ordinary URL rather than a workload identifier.
The subject belongs to a trust domain for which no bundle is admitted.
The workload ID includes a forbidden query component.
The signature bytes are changed after issuance.
A successfully authenticated client has a revoked application grant.
A valid identity is mapped to a different tenant operation.
A valid identity is offered for a purpose outside its application grant.
Another genuine workload is not the sender permitted by this case.
An old token remains signed while its signing key is retired from the bundle.
A new signing key is published before a new token is consumed.
A declared not-before interval has not started.
The admitted library is asked to parse an oversized token.
A duplicate operation is authenticated but must not be applied twice.
A named human owner exists but useful reviewer capacity is unavailable.

selected_signature_profile: RS256 only; other supported SPIFFE signature suites are not tested
